questions.prompt: How does partitioning differ from replication?
options: Partitioning copies data; replication splits it
Partitioning puts different subsets on different machines; replication puts the same data on several

questions.prompt: An overloaded partition that gets more than its share of load is a hot ______. (one word)

options: Range scans are efficient because keys stay sorted within a partition

questions.prompt: Sensor readings are keyed by timestamp in a range-partitioned store. What goes wrong?
options: All of today's writes land on one partition

questions.prompt: A language's built-in hash() is a good choice for picking partitions.
What does hash partitioning give up?
options: Efficient range queries, since adjacent keys scatter
